how_counted: Counties count early voting and Election Day ballots first and mail ballots later.
count_order: Early voting and Election Day first; mail and absentee later (Election Law 9-200, 9-208).
vote_types: no on the state page. New York counts early voting and Election Day first and mail/absentee later (the page cites Election Law 9-200, 9-208; certification within 25 days for a general). NYC's ED-level recaps list lines by election district only.

certify.body: the New York State Board of Canvassers
certify.rule: In years without presidential electors, meets on or before the 15th day after the election (N.Y. Elec. Law 9-216); counties send their certified statements within 25 days (9-214).
certify.source: NCSL, 'Election Certification Deadlines' (www.ncsl.org/elections-and-campaigns/certification-deadlines), read 2026-10-10; secondary: a summary of each state's law, not the law itself

terms: the page's 'Statement on the Unofficial Nature of Election Night Results'; no terms of use for reuse
scout_blocked: nyenr.elections.ny.gov and elections.ny.gov answer scripts with a Cloudflare challenge (403); must not be worked around. The Browser pane passes it like any browser.
scout_plan: Blocked to scripts on the night. Options, in order: (1) John keeps the state ENR page open in his own browser and saves it (Save as, HTML) into a watched folder every few minutes, or the Browser pane on his computer saves it, and the updater parses the saved copy; this works the same way as Minnesota's hand-saved files; (2) read New York City's enr.boenyc.gov directly (it answered scripts) for the city's congressional and legislative districts; (3) final figures from the Board's certified workbook weeks later. Ask John whether reading the state page through the Browser pane on election night is acceptable; it is a public page a browser opens normally.
